claims.text: The initially solid Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles are homogeneous solid solutions before annealing.
Premelting and melting behavior in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by the onset of nanoscale elemental segregation.
Mild sub-premelting annealing promotes incipient atomic segregation without causing full melting.
Mild annealing facilitates atomic diffusion in these nanoparticles.
Annealing-induced diffusion produces nanoscale chemical inhomogeneities.
The chemical inhomogeneities can include copper-rich or other lower-melting clusters.
Locally segregated regions have lower melting temperatures than the homogeneous alloy.
Lower-melting segregated regions act as initiation or nucleation sites for melting.
Melting initiated at segregated regions reduces the effective melting-onset temperature of the entire nanoparticle.
Pre-annealed nanoparticles will have a lower measured melting onset than non-annealed homogeneous nanoparticles under identical thermal ramps.
Pre-annealing may broaden the melting transition relative to the baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies when atomic mobility permits limited segregation but not complete phase separation.
The melting-onset shift depends on annealing temperature, annealing time, and diffusion kinetics.
